newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore sentences official to jail for corruption.
newsitem.headline: Singapore sentences official to jail for corruption.

text.p: A Singapore court sentenced an official of the government's investment arm to nine years in jail and a fine of Singapore $2.4 million (US$1.7 million) for corruption on Monday, prosecutors said.
Taw Cheng Kiang, a regional manager for the Government of Singapore Investment Corporation (GIC), appealed against his conviction and remained free on bail of S$5 million, state television said.
Prosecutors told Reuters the fine amounted to the sum Taw was charged with receiving in kickbacks for steering government money into selected shares.
The GIC is responsible for managing part of Singapore's huge foreign reserves of more than S$100 billion and holds stocks and bonds in 25 countries.

Taw was found guilty of receiving bribes from Kevin Lee Kwok-wing, then managing director of Hong Kong asset management firm Rockefeller & Co (Far East), to buy specific shares between 1991 and August 1996.
Singapore is tough on corruption and is typically rated in surveys as one of the least corrupt places to do business in Asia.
